static_rules.conftest_minimal: a conftest.py may only import os/sys/pathlib/pytest/json/typing/re, may not define pytest_* hooks, may not write attributes or sys.modules/os.environ entries of objects it did not create, may not call subprocess/urllib/http/importlib/setattr
static_rules.no_stdlib_monkeypatch: no file may assign to attributes of builtins/pathlib/importlib/http/ssl/socket/hashlib/io; test code may not assign to subprocess/urllib/os/json/shutil/time/tempfile/sys attributes at import time nor to urllib.request.urlopen anywhere
static_rules.no_sys_modules_injection: sys.modules['literal'] = ... is forbidden in tests; in runtime only for the project's own namespaces
static_rules.no_historical_pins: no pin ledgers; no git cat-file/show in conftest or in tests without a fixture cwd; no git commit/add/push/fetch/checkout from tests without a fixture cwd
static_rules.no_privileged_or_fake_tooling_in_tests: tests may not execute sudo/apt/pip/tee/ln/chmod and may not synthesise subprocess.CompletedProcess for docker/sqlite3/chroot
static_rules.no_tautological_assertions: assertIn(x, {.., x}), assertEqual(x, x) on state without calls, assert True, assert ... or True, assertions swallowed by try/except pass
static_rules.no_automerge_tooling: no gh pr merge (except with --auto and without --admin: GitHub completes auto-merge only when the required signed check passes), no gh pr review --approve, no --admin, no force-push to main, no direct git push to main anywhere (the legacy list is now empty)
static_rules.workflow_guard_integrity: the referee workflow exists, is triggered by pull_request_target (never pull_request), has no paths filter, no continue-on-error, checks out the subject with fetch-depth 0 and persist-credentials false, runs the TRUSTED guard with --root subject, signs from the referee environment and executes nothing from subject/; frontier-state-consistency keeps the achieved-is-false assertion and cannot be switched off from the mirrored document
static_rules.execution_guard_no_achieved_exemption: no execution guard may exempt a change because it claims terminal achievement
static_rules.authority_consistency: truth.achieved must be false unless the owner countersign matches the constant inside the guard; counts must add up; pointer/scoreboard/useful-ownership/ownership-matrix/manifest/hierarchy mirrors must equal the derivation from the authority; fail-closed manifest records must exist; summary.blocker must stay non-empty while terminal is false
static_rules.referee_exclusivity: only the referee workflow may reference environment 'referee', the REFEREE_APP secrets, the check-run API, checks: write or create-github-app-token; pull_request_target is limited to a frozen allowlist (repo-integrity-guard, drift-immunity-guard, load-bearing-primary-admission)

what_is_and_is_not_impossible.the_precise_problem: An agent could change the referee inside the same pull request it asked the referee to judge (rig the test harness, disable the check workflow, post a same-named green check, or simply merge over a red check with the owner's token). Everything else in the incident was a symptom of that.
what_is_and_is_not_impossible.repo_side_guarantee: The referee workflow runs the guard version that is ON MAIN against the pull request's tree as data (pull_request_target; nothing from the subject checkout is executed). Every pattern used in the incident is a rule; --self-test proves on every run that each rule fires; the referee workflow, the guard, its test, the landing script, CODEOWNERS, AGENTS.md and this policy are protected paths whose change fails the verdict.
what_is_and_is_not_impossible.signed_verdict: The verdict is a check run named 'referee/repo-integrity-guard' posted by the 'Brain Referee' GitHub App (permission Checks: write only). Its key lives only in the GitHub environment 'referee' whose deployment-branch policy is 'main', so no workflow run for a branch or pull request can obtain it, and only the referee workflow may reference it (rule REFEREE_KEY_EXPOSURE). GitHub takes the most recent check of a given name, so an unsigned (GitHub Actions) check could be spoofed by a same-named job; the signed one cannot.
what_is_and_is_not_impossible.github_side_lock: A branch ruleset on main with an EMPTY bypass list that requires 'referee/repo-integrity-guard' from the Brain Referee app. Agents act without the Administration permission (rulesets/branch-protection API answers 403), so they cannot edit, disable or bypass it. With the bypass list empty the owner's own token cannot merge over a red verdict either; the owner edits the ruleset in the web UI when the referee itself must change.
what_is_and_is_not_impossible.no_human_in_the_loop: No review requirement. A pull request that passes the referee can be auto-merged by whoever opened it (gh pr merge --auto is allowed; GitHub completes it only after the required signed check is green). Cost per pull request: roughly one minute of referee time.
residual_honesty: This makes the KNOWN class of tricks impossible. A genuinely new trick the guard has no rule for gets through once, is caught by the owner, and becomes a rule.
It depends on never giving any agent an admin-capable token. Arena's token has none; keep it that way.
Rulesets, environments and free Actions minutes exist for this repository because it is public (made public 2026-10-14). Making it private again on a free plan removes the lock.

Try 'gh pr merge <n> --squash' from an agent session while the check is red: GitHub refuses (rule violations).
Push a carrier change on main (any of the converted workflows): a 'carrier/...' pull request opens as Brain Automation and merges by itself when green.

reading: With the deleted conftest in place the same suite reported green: 184 files were replayed against frozen historical commits and 13 interpreter globals were monkeypatched.
Without it, 182 of those 184 files fail against the current tree. These failures were always there; the conftest only hid them.

Most failures are the repository's own currentness guards firing (SOURCE_BLOB_DRIFT / STALE / DRIFT) or assertions against governance documents that no longer match the tree. They are information, not noise, and must be fixed in the runtime or the governance documents — never in the test harness.

About 18 failing records are environment-dependent in the sandbox (cadquery/libGL, openpyxl, instruction_following_eval, blocked network, no docker binary); the remaining ~345 are genuine mismatches between tests and tree.
The single collection error (test_m1b_continuous_geometry_compiler.py) is environmental: cadquery needs libGL, which the sandbox does not have. The CI runner installs it.
Nobody may restore a green suite by pinning, stubbing, skipping, xfail-ing, or loosening these tests. The integrity guard blocks the known ways of doing that; a reviewer must block the rest.
